Here, the denominator is the imaginary number $4\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+4\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-4\text{i},$ or simply $-4\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-4\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-12+5\text{i}}{4\text{i}} & =\frac{-12+5\text{i}}{4\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-4\text{i}}{-4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{48\text{i}-20{\text{i}}^{2}}{-16{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{48\text{i}-20(-1)}{-16(-1)} \\  & =\frac{20+48\text{i}}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{20+48\text{i}}{16} & =\frac{20}{16}+\frac{48}{16}\text{i} \\  & =(\frac{5}{4})+(3)\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
